title: How Works Better keeps an enquiry from disappearing
excerpt: A first-hand account of the enquiry system I built for this website: saving the brief, showing a reference and keeping personal follow-up distinct from a receipt.
content:
Documented implementation · Works Better's own website · verified 2 October 2026. This account describes what I built here. It is not an external client case study or a claim about measured sales improvement.

The problem I designed for

A visitor describes a business problem and presses send. They need to know whether the enquiry was saved, and I need the context to respond. A successful-looking screen alone would not establish either.

The form asks about the process, existing tools and desired result, with optional business, operating-mode and discovery-source details. It helps someone describe the need in their own words; technical terminology is not required.

What I built

  1. Check the brief. Required fields and a minimum brief length are validated before submission.
  2. Save the enquiry. A confirmed saved response includes a reference for the visitor. It is separate from an email reply.
  3. Notify the owner. An email notification goes to the Works Better inbox, which I monitor personally.
  4. Follow up as a person. I review the need and discuss fit. Scope and fees are agreed before paid work.

The receipt says the brief is saved and that a reply has not been sent yet. This system does not send an AI-written reply, qualify a sales opportunity automatically or commit someone to a project.

Keep an uncertain submission visible

If the browser cannot confirm the save or the confirmation takes too long, it keeps the written details and offers a retry or email route. A retry of an unchanged brief uses the same request identifier to help avoid duplicate records.

Saving the enquiry, sending a notification and receiving a personal reply are separate events. A receipt cannot establish that every later step has happened.

What was actually checked

On 2 October 2026, one clearly labelled synthetic release enquiry received a saved response and on-screen reference. An independent storage check found its record; the notification was recorded as sent, and I confirmed receiving it in the configured inbox.

Separate browser checks covered validation, success and error states. Later browser tests intercepted submissions so they did not send additional notifications. The client measurement check recorded one successful-submission event for the release test; that does not by itself prove processing in an Analytics report.

The synthetic test is excluded from lead and opportunity totals. These checks establish the tested handling, not improved conversion, guaranteed email delivery or a response-time commitment.

Where this fits with the AI examples

This enquiry system is an implemented website tool, not the fictional AI enquiry demonstration. For an AI-assisted approach, explore the staff approval and separate customer-confirmation decisions.

My consulting site has a separate first-hand account of an Outlook-to-CRM workflow I built. It describes customer context, a reviewed reply and connected follow-through while keeping the organisation private.

Make the next step clear in your business

Tell me where requests get lost, which tools your team uses and what needs to happen next. I reply personally and agree scope and fees before any paid work.
